title: The Burnt Contact
premise: Mirabel Okafor, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call she couldn't save, has spent three years buried in a quiet bureau desk, hiding a past identity and a lover she abandoned for duty. When her dead handler emails a meeting invitation for tomorrow, Mirabel is pulled into a conspiracy: an attack on a city water facility staged to look like an industrial accident, orchestrated by the same network that once owned her. To stop it she must resurrect the self she buried, trust the lover who believes she betrayed him, and decide whether saving hundreds is worth exposing every lie she's built. In the end, Mirabel stops the attack by surrendering her anonymity to the world—and to him—choosing love and truth over the invisibility that kept her safe.
about_author: Coral Brightwater is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people talk their way back from the edge. She writes thrillers about the moments when words are the only weapon left.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Three years into bureaucratic exile, she receives an email from Daniel Reyes—her handler, dead eleven months—inviting her to meet tomorrow at noon. The message contains a phrase only he knew from her old life. She packs the go-bag she swore she'd never use again. Emotional beat: dread cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Knew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the meeting site she finds no Daniel—only a burner phone with a recording of his voice, made days before his death, warning of an attack 'dressed as an accident' and naming the Meridian Water Facility. Someone is watching her; she spots a tail and loses them using tradecraft she'd promised to forget. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Lie Polished
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with a flashback to her years undercover inside the Halcyon network, where she fell for Tomas Vidal, the network's logistics man who never learned her real name. Present-day: her bureau supervisor notices her digging and warns her off. Beat: the cost of the double life pressing down again.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Mirabel tracks Tomas, now living quietly under his own name, running a marina repair shop. He reacts to seeing her with fury—her disappearance after the operation collapsed got two assets killed and left him holding suspicion. He refuses to help until she shows him Daniel's recording. Beat: anger curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He walks Mirabel through what he knows: Halcyon's remnant cell has contracted a chemical engineer and scheduled a chlorine release at Meridian during a maintenance window, timed so casualties read as negligence. He realizes Daniel must have been feeding information to someone inside the cell. Beat: the scale of the threat becomes real.

chapters.title: The Engineer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The chemical engineer, Ada Lindqvist, has vanished—but her teenage daughter hasn't. Mirabel talks her way into the girl's confidence at a bus depot, learning Ada was coerced via threats against her family. Negotiation instincts reawaken. Meanwhile the tail from chapter two photographs them. Beat: competence returning like blood to a numb limb.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following Daniel's recorded instructions, she retrieves his hidden files and discovers the truth: Daniel faked his death to infiltrate the cell, and the person who exposed him is Bureau Deputy Director Hale—the supervisor who 'warned her off.' Hale has been protecting Halcyon remnants for years. Beat: betrayal at the institutional level; nowhere safe.

chapters.title: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. With Hale hunting them, Mirabel and Tomas go dark, pressuring Ada through her daughter to stall the attack while they plan to breach Meridian's control systems. Tomas admits he never stopped looking for her. They cross a line together the night before the operation. Beat: love rekindled under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Climax. Mirabel's POV. During the maintenance window, Mirabel enters Meridian posing as an inspector while Tomas cuts external power triggers. Hale arrives personally to ensure the attack proceeds. Mirabel negotiates—not with a hostage-taker but with Ada at gunpoint, talking her through disabling the release valve while Hale closes in. Tomas takes a bullet shielding her. Beat: everything she is, spent at once.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Resolution. Mirabel testifies, burning her cover identity permanently and ending Hale's career; the Bureau offers her a new one, and she declines. She visits Daniel's grave, finally grieving him. At the marina, Tomas, recovering, asks who she'll be now. She says her real name out loud for the first time in years. Beat: identity chosen, not survived.
